title: Review RMS open message panel for active errors/warnings and alarm history (past 24–48 hours)
summary: Use the RMS / fleet status UI open message panel to view pending messages containing active errors or warnings, and review the alarm history window covering roughly the past 24–48 hours.
when_to_use: When you need to quickly check whether the fleet has pending active error/warning messages and to review recent alarm history over the last ~24–48 hours.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Open the RMS / fleet status UI and review the open message panel for pending active errors/warnings and the alarm history time window.

visual_references.description: Map Monitor Message Panel frame showing the open message panel area and related counts (active robots, charging, AGV faults dropdown, disconnected count) used to locate the open message panel and interpret what is shown.

steps.title: Open the RMS / fleet status UI map monitor summary area
steps.purpose: Get to the area where the open message panel and alarm history are available.
steps.instruction: In the RMS / fleet status UI (rms_ui), navigate to the map monitor summary area where the open message panel is located.
steps.expected_result: You are viewing the map monitor summary area that contains the open message panel.
steps.healthy_condition: The map monitor summary area is visible and the open message panel region is accessible/expandable.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot locate the open message panel region in the RMS / fleet status UI.

actions.label: Locate open message panel region
actions.exact_action: Open the RMS / fleet status UI (RMS / fleet status UI / map monitor summary area).

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “The first one is the open message panel…”

steps.title: Expand/open the open message panel to view pending active errors/warnings
steps.purpose: Identify pending messages that contain active errors or warnings.
steps.instruction: Open/expand the open message panel in the RMS / fleet status UI to display pending messages containing active errors or warnings.
steps.expected_result: The open message panel shows a list of pending messages that contain active errors or warnings.
steps.healthy_condition: Pending messages are visible in the open message panel, and you can read the active error/warning entries from the panel contents.
steps.failure_condition: The open message panel does not show pending active errors/warnings when the system is known to be faulting, or you cannot determine what the active errors/warnings are from the panel contents.

actions.label: Open message panel
actions.exact_action: Find the “open message panel” area and open it to view pending messages that contain active errors or warnings.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the message panel shows active errors/warnings that require attention and you cannot identify the fault details from the panel contents.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “pending messages that is containing active errors or warnings on the system, you… can open that message panel to see that as well as the history of the alarms…”

steps.title: Review alarm history window in the same panel (past ~24–48 hours)
steps.purpose: Confirm the alarm history time window and review recent alarm entries.
steps.instruction: Within the same open message panel view, review the alarm history list and confirm the displayed history window corresponds to roughly the past 24–48 hours.
steps.expected_result: The alarm history list is visible and the time window shown corresponds to roughly the past 24–48 hours.
steps.healthy_condition: Alarm history entries are present for the expected recent window (about 24–48 hours).
steps.failure_condition: The alarm history window shown does not correspond to the past ~24–48 hours, or the alarm history cannot be reviewed due to missing/unclear window context.

actions.label: Check alarm history window
actions.exact_action: In the same panel, review the alarm history list and confirm the history window shown corresponds to the past ~24–48 hours.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: “…history of the alarms that it generated over maybe like the past 2448 hours.”

steps.title: Stop and escalate when panel contents are insufficient to identify fault details
steps.purpose: Ensure unresolved active errors/warnings are escalated when fault details cannot be determined from the panel.
steps.instruction: If the open message panel indicates active errors/warnings requiring attention but you cannot identify the fault details from the panel contents, stop further interpretation and escalate.
steps.expected_result: You have identified the condition where fault details are not determinable from the panel contents and you initiate escalation.
steps.healthy_condition: Either (a) fault details are identifiable from the panel contents, or (b) escalation is initiated when they are not.
steps.failure_condition: Continuing without escalation despite active errors/warnings requiring attention and insufficient fault detail visibility in the panel.

actions.label: Escalate
actions.exact_action: Stop and escalate if the message panel shows active errors/warnings that require attention and you cannot identify the fault details from the panel contents.

stop_or_escalate_if: Active errors/warnings require attention AND fault details cannot be identified from the panel contents.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Candidate escalation condition: “Stop and escalate if the message panel shows active errors/warnings that require attention and you cannot identify the fault details from the panel contents.”

success_criteria: Open message panel shows pending messages containing active errors or warnings (when present).
Alarm history window shown in the panel corresponds to roughly the past 24–48 hours.
healthy_conditions: Open message panel displays pending active error/warning messages.
Alarm history entries are shown for the expected recent window (~24–48 hours).
failure_conditions: No pending active errors/warnings are shown when the system is known to be faulting.
You cannot determine what the active errors/warnings are from the open message panel contents.
Alarm history window shown does not correspond to roughly the past 24–48 hours.
escalation_guidance: Escalate when active errors/warnings require attention but fault details cannot be identified from the open message panel contents.
